steps.body: The full pipeline: **find the LCD, convert each fraction, combine tops, simplify.** 3/x + 2/(x + 1) over LCD x(x + 1): tops become 3(x + 1) and 2x, so the sum is (3x + 3 + 2x)/(x(x + 1)) = **(5x + 3)/(x(x + 1))**.

widget.prompt: In 3/x + 2/(x + 1) over the LCD x(x + 1), the first fraction's numerator becomes:

options.label: 3(x + 1)
options.feedback: Right — 3/x gains the missing factor (x + 1) on top.

options.label: 3x
options.feedback: x is ALREADY under the 3 — the missing factor is (x + 1), which multiplies the top.
The bottom grew by (x + 1); the top must match, or the value changes.

options.label: 3x(x + 1)
options.feedback: Only the MISSING factor joins the top — the x stays downstairs.

steps.body: Subtraction adds the Chapter-opening trap on top of the pipeline. 5/(x − 2) − 3/x over x(x − 2): (5x − 3(x − 2))/(x(x − 2)) = (5x − 3x + 6)/(x(x − 2)) = **(2x + 6)/(x(x − 2))**. Distribute the −3 into BOTH terms: −3 · −2 = **+6**.

explanationVariants: Convert both, then the minus distributes into 2(x + 1).

commonBuilds.feedback: The −2 multiplies the WHOLE (x + 1): −2x − 2, so the constant is −2.
Unlike fractions don't subtract level-by-level — convert to the LCD x(x + 1) first.
The 2/x fraction converts by (x + 1): its top becomes 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2, not just 2.

widget.missFeedback: Convert both to the LCD x(x + 1): 4x/(x(x + 1)) − 2(x + 1)/(x(x + 1)), then subtract the tops.

widget.prompt: Check 3/x + 2/(x + 1) = (5x + 3)/(x(x + 1)) at x = 2: compute 3/2 + 2/3 as a fraction a/6. What is a?

commonErrors.feedback: 3/2 + 2/3 = 9/6 + 4/6 = 13/6 — convert BOTH to sixths before adding tops.
6 is the DENOMINATOR of the sum — the combined NUMERATOR is 9 + 4 = 13.

explanationVariants: LCD (x − 3)(x + 3): tops x(x + 3) and 6·1... careful — 6/(x² − 9) already sits on the LCD; x/(x − 3) gains (x + 3): (x² + 3x + 6)/((x − 3)(x + 3)).
Only the first fraction converts; then add tops.

commonBuilds.feedback: The first top converts to x(x + 3) = x² + 3x — it doesn't stay a bare x.
x² − 9 contributes no second (x − 3) — the LCD is (x − 3)(x + 3), single copies.
Denominators never ADD — build the LCD and convert the tops.

widget.missFeedback: Factor x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3), convert x/(x − 3) by (x + 3), and add the tops over the LCD.

explanationVariants: Symmetric tops: the constants cancel, the x's double.

commonBuilds.feedback: The converted tops are (x + 1) and (x − 1) — they sum to 2x, not 2.
The bottom is the PRODUCT (x − 1)(x + 1) = x² − 1, not the sum 2x.
The +1 and −1 cancel in the sum: (x + 1) + (x − 1) = 2x exactly.

widget.missFeedback: Convert both to the LCD (x − 1)(x + 1) = x² − 1, then add the tops: (x + 1) + (x − 1) = 2x.

explanationVariants: Convert, subtract with the distributed minus, factor the 2.

commonBuilds.feedback: The minus reaches the +2: 3x − x − 2 gives −2, factoring as 2(x MINUS 1).
1/x converts by (x + 2): the subtracted top is the whole (x + 2), not a bare 1.
Unlike bottoms can't subtract directly — the LCD x(x + 2) hosts the combined tops.

widget.missFeedback: Over the LCD x(x + 2): 3x − (x + 2) = 2x − 2, which factors as 2(x − 1).

hints: LCD: x(x + 2); tops convert to 3x and (x + 2).

steps.body: LCD, convert, combine, simplify — with the minus fully distributed.
takeaways: Each top gains exactly its missing factors.
A fraction already on the LCD converts by 1 — leave it alone.
Factor the combined numerator; cancellations hide there.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: the GRAPHS — asymptotes, holes, and the reciprocal shape.

concept.body: One conversion, one add: 1/x + 1/(2x). LCD 2x: the first top converts to 2, the second stays 1.

options.label: 2/(3x)
options.feedback: The LCD is 2x (highest power of each factor) — tops become 2 and 1, summing to 3.

options.label: 1/(3x)... adding bottoms
options.feedback: Denominators never add — convert to the LCD 2x, then add tops: 3/(2x).
